## Intro to similarity
2 figures are <i>similar</i> if 1 can be obtained from the other by sliding, spinning, flipping, or blowing up (recall they would be congruent if we can do any of these except blowing up). If 2 figures are similar, then their corresponding angles have the same measure, and the ratio between 2 corresponding side lengths is constant (in the case of congruence, this ratio is 1).
Below, figure $ABCD$ is similar to figure $EFGH$.
We write $ABCD \sim EFGH$. Just as with congruence, we are careful to line up corresponding vertices. Thus, $m \angle A=m \angle E$, $m \angle B=m \angle F$, $m \angle C=m \angle G$, and $m \angle D=m \angle H$. Further, $AB/EF=BC/FG=CD/GH=DA/HE=AC/EG=BD/FH$.
As with congruence, our main focus is on triangles.

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = np.ones((700, 700, 3), dtype=np.uint8) * 255
a=(100,300)
b=(400,150)
c=(550,300)
d=(400,600)
e=(200,300)
f=(400,200)
g=(500,300)
h=(400,500)
draw_path(img,a,b,c,d,a)
draw_path(img,e,f,g,h,e)
for j,lbl in enumerate('DAEBGCH'):
    p=globals()[lbl.lower()]
    x,y=(0,-10) if j%2 else (-25,20)
    cv2.putText(img,lbl,(p[0]+x,p[1]+y),font,0.6,color,2)
cv2.putText(img,'F',(f[0]-10,f[1]+25),font,0.6,color,2)
show_geometry_image(img)
```

## AA similarity
If we can show all angles between 2 figures are the same, and all corresponding side lengths have the same ratio, then we have that the 2 figures are similar. Again as with congruence, we can get away with showing less, especially with triangles.

::: {#lem-5.aa}

Angle-Angle aka <i>AA similarity</i>: If 2 angles in a triangle have the same measures as 2 angles in another, then the 2 triangles are similar.
Ie, given triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$, if $m \angle A=m \angle D$ and $m \angle B=m \angle E$, then $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$.

:::

::: {.proof}

We are done if $AB=DE$ since then we actually have $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ by ASA congruence @lem-3.asa. So assume without loss of generality that $DE>AB$.
Let point $G$ be such that $AB=DG$. Use the parallel postulate to draw the line through $G$ parallel to $\overline{EF}$, let point $H$ be its intersection with $\overline{DF}$.
Then $m \angle B=m \angle E=m \angle DGH$ by @lem-2.7, so $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DGH$ by ASA congruence @lem-3.asa. So it is enough to show that $\triangle DGH \sim \triangle DEF$.
$m \angle F=m \angle DHG$ by @lem-2.5, so we just need to show the 3 pairs of sides have the same ratio. $[GHE]=[GHF]$ by @lem-4.3, so $[DHE]=[DGH]+[GHE]=[DGH]+[GHF]=[DGF]$, so $DG/DE=[DGH]/[DHE]=[DGH]/[DGF]=DH/DF$ by 2 applications of @lem-4.3. Thus, $AB/DE=AC/DF$.
By an analogous argument, we also get $AB/DE=BC/EF$ (ie, start by 'superimposing' $\overline{BC}$ onto $\overline{EF}$).

:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = np.ones((500, 700, 3), dtype=np.uint8) * 255
a=(400,100)
b=(200,300)
c=(500,300)
d,g,h=a,b,c
e=(100,400)
f=(550,400)
draw_path(img,a,b,c,a)
cv2.ellipse(img,a,(25,25),0,63,135,color,thickness=1) #angle marker
add_tick(img,a,b)
img1=img.copy()
draw_path(img1,g,e,f,h)
cv2.arrowedLine(img1, (350, e[1]), (360, e[1]), color, thickness=1, tipLength=1.0) #parallel markers
cv2.arrowedLine(img1, (350, b[1]), (360, b[1]), color, thickness=1, tipLength=1.0)
for j,lbl in enumerate('ABCDFEHG'):
    p=globals()[lbl.lower()]
    x=img if j<3 else img1
    q=-20 if j%2 else 10
    cv2.putText(x,lbl,(p[0]+q,p[1]),font,0.6,color,2)
imgt=img.copy()
img1t=img1.copy()
for q in [img,img1]:
    cv2.line(q, (400,120), (400,130), color, thickness=1)
    cv2.ellipse(q,b,(25,25),0,315,360,color,thickness=1)
cv2.ellipse(img1,e,(25,25),0,315,360,color,thickness=1)
show_many_images(img,img1,nrows=2)
```

AA similarity is the most common way to show that 2 triangles are similar. AA similarity is special to triangles and does not extend to figures with more sides. For instance, given figures $ABCD$ and $EFGH$, if we know all their angles are right angles, they need not be similar since $ABCD$ can be a square, while $EFGH$ can be a non-square rectangle.<br>
We now consider 3 common scenarios where similar triangles are encountered.

::: {#lem-5.sim.plel2}

Below, $\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE$ if and only if $\overline{AB}\parallel \overline{CD}$.

:::

::: {.proof}

$\overline{AB}\parallel \overline{CD}$ if and only if $m \angle A=m \angle D$ by @lem-2.7. Combined with $m \angle AEB=m \angle DEC$ by @lem-2.3, this is if and only if $\triangle ABE \sim \triangle DCE$ by @lem-5.aa.

:::

A common mistake in this scenario is to say $AE/CE=BE/DE$.


Given $a,b \geq 0$, their <i>geometric mean</i> is $\sqrt{ab}$. Geometric means often appear in lengths from right triangles.

::: {#lem-5.sim.right}

If $\triangle ABC$ is a right triangle with $m \angle ABC=90^\circ$, and point $D$ is on $\overline{AC}$ such that $\overline{BD}$ is the altitude corresponding to base $\overline{AC}$, then $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADB \sim \triangle BDC$.
In particular, $(AB)^2=AD \cdot AC$ and $(BD)^2=AD \cdot CD$.

:::

::: {.proof}

We have $m \angle ABC=m \angle ADB=m \angle BDC=90^\circ$ and $m \angle A=m \angle CBD$ by @lem-2.5. Thus, $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADB \sim \triangle BDC$ by AA similarity @lem-5.aa.
In particular, $AC/AB=AB/AD$ $\leftrightarrow$ $(AB)^2=AD \cdot AC$ and $AD/BD=BD/CD$ $\leftrightarrow$ $(BD)^2=AD \cdot CD$.

:::

## SAS similarity

::: {#lem-5.sas}

Side-angle-side aka <i>SAS similarity</i>: if 2 side lengths of 1 triangle are in the same ratio as 2 sides of another, and the angle these 2 sides form has the same measure, then the triangles are similar.
Ie, given $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$ as below, where $AB/DE=AC/DF$ (equivalently $AB/AC=DE/DF$) and $m \angle A=m \angle D$, then $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$.
Further, in the bottom figure, the following are equivalent:

- $\triangle DEF \sim \triangle DGH$.
- $\overline{EF}\parallel \overline{GH}$.
- $DG/GE=DH/DF$.

:::

A common mistake is to say $DG/GE=GH/EF$.

::: {.proof}

$\overline{EF}\parallel \overline{GH}$ if and only if $m \angle DGH=m \angle E$ by @lem-2.7, which is if and only if $\triangle DEF \sim \triangle DGH$ by AA similarity @lem-5.aa since they share $\angle D$.<br>
To show SAS similarity, we start the same way as we did to prove @lem-5.aa. We are done if $AB=DE$ (and hence $AC=DF$ by hypothesis) since then we actually have $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ by SAS congruence. So assume without loss of generality that $DE>AB$.
Let point $G$ be such that $AB=DG$. Use the parallel postulate to draw the line through $G$ parallel to $\overline{EF}$, let point $H$ be its intersection with $\overline{DF}$.
Then $\triangle DGH \sim \triangle DEF$, so $AC/DF=AB/DE=DG/DE=DH/DF$, ie $AC=DH$. By SAS congruence, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DGH \sim \triangle DEF$. Thus, $m \angle B=m \angle DGH=m \angle E$, and $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$ as desired.<br>
Finally, $DG/GE=DF/FH$ if and only if $DG/DE=DF/DH$ by algebra, which is if and only if $\triangle DEF \sim \triangle DGH$ by SAS similarity.

:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = imgt.copy()
img1=img1t.copy()
for q in [img,img1]:
    for j in [-5,5]:
        add_tick(q,(400,100),(500,300),offset_px=j)
show_many_images(img,img1,nrows=2)
```

## SSS similarity

::: {#lem-5.sss}

Side-side-side aka <i>SSS similarity</i>: if each side length of 1 triangle is the same multiple as the corresponding side length of another, then the triangles are similar.
Ie, given $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$, where $AB/DE=AC/DF=BC/EF$, then $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$.

:::

SSS similarity is less useful than SAS and esp AA similarity.

## Problem solving with similarity

::: {#lem-5.5sim.area}

Given that $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$, with points $P,Q$ on $\overleftrightarrow{BC}, \overleftrightarrow{EF}$ are the feet of altitudes $\overline{AP}, \overline{DQ}$ (resp), and $k:=AB/DE$, then $k=AP/DQ$ and $[ABC]/[DEF]=k^2$.
Knowing the ratio for any quantity, we can derive the ratio for any other (any of the 3 sides, altitudes, or the area).
In words, for 2 similar triangles, the ratio between any 2 corresponding altitudes is the ratio of any 2 corresponding side lengths, and this ratio gets squared for area.

:::

::: {.proof}

Since $m \angle APB=m \angle DQE=90^\circ$ and $m \angle B=m \angle E$, $\triangle ABP \sim \triangle DEQ$ by AA similarity @lem-5.aa. So $AP/DQ=AB/DE=k$. Since $BC/EF=AB/DE=k$ too, by @lem-4.tri.area
$$\frac{[ABC]}{[DEF]}= \frac{AP \cdot BC/2}{DQ \cdot EF/2}= \frac{AP}{BQ}\cdot \frac{BC}{EF}=k^2$$

:::

## Construction: angles and parallel lines

::: {#exm-5.angle}

Given $\angle A$ and a ray with origin $B$, draw a line/ ray/ segment thru $B$ such that the resulting angle has the same measure as $\angle A$.<br>
Draw (part of) a circle with center $A$ (and any radius), let points $C,D$ be the intersection with the 2 sides of $\angle A$.
Draw $\odot B$ with the same radius, let point $E$ be the intersection with the ray with origin $B$.
Draw $\odot E$ with radius $CD$, let point $F$ be its intersection with $\odot B$ (pick any such point). Then $m \angle EBF=m \angle A$.

::: {.proof}

By construction, $AC=BE=AD=BF$, and $CD=EF$, so $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle BEF$ by SSS congruence @lem-3.sss, and $m \angle EBF=m \angle A$ by CPCTC.

::: 

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = np.ones((400, 500, 3), dtype=np.uint8) * 255
a=(100,300); b=a
c=(350,300); e=c
d=(300,150); f=d
cv2.arrowedLine(img, a, (400, 300), color, tipLength=0.02, thickness=2)
cv2.arrowedLine(img, a, (340, 120), color, tipLength=0.02, thickness=2)
cv2.line(img,c,d, color, thickness=1)
cv2.ellipse(img,a,(250,250),0,315,375,color,thickness=1)
add_tick(img,a,c)
add_tick(img,a,d)
add_tick(img,c,d,offset_px=5)
add_tick(img,c,d,offset_px=-5)
img1=img.copy()
cv2.ellipse(img1,e,(158,158),0,225,270,color,thickness=1)
cv2.putText(img, "A", (a[0], a[1]+20), font, 0.6, color, 2)
cv2.putText(img1,"B", (b[0], b[1]+20), font, 0.6, color, 2)
cv2.putText(img, "C", (c[0], c[1]+20), font, 0.6, color, 2)
cv2.putText(img1,"E", (e[0], e[1]+20), font, 0.6, color, 2)
cv2.putText(img, "D", (d[0]-10, d[1]-10), font, 0.6, color, 2)
cv2.putText(img1,"F", (f[0]-10, f[1]-10), font, 0.6, color, 2)
show_many_images(img,img1)
```

::: {#exm-5.parallel}

Given a line k and a point $A$ not on k, draw a line thru $A$ parallel to k.<br>
Draw any line thru $A$ that intersects k, say at point $B$. Let $C$ be any other point on k.
Draw a line $\overleftrightarrow{AD}$ such that $\overleftrightarrow{AD}$ forms the same angle with it as it does with line k using @exm-5.angle.
Then $\overleftrightarrow{AD}\parallel \overleftrightarrow{BC}$ by @lem-2.7.

:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
```

::: {#exm-5.trisect}

Trisect a given segment $\overline{AB}$, ie split it into 3 segments of equal length.<br>
Draw a ray with origin at point $A$ (and does not hit $B$). Let $C$ be any point on the ray. Find points $D,E$ on the ray such that $AC=CD=DE$.
Draw $\overline{BE}$, then lines thru $C,D$ parallel to it using @exm-5.parallel. Let $F,G$ be their points of intersection with $\overline{AB}$. Then $AF=FG=GB$.

:::

::: {.proof}

$AF/AB=AC/AE=1/3$ and $AG/AB=AD/AE=2/3$ by @lem-5.sas, so $AF=FG=GB$.

:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = np.ones((500, 500, 3), dtype=np.uint8) * 255
cv2.line(img, (100,100),(100,400), color, thickness=2)
cv2.arrowedLine(img,(100,100),(450,450), color, thickness=1, tipLength=0.02)
pts=[(100,100)]
for q in [150,250,350]:
    cv2.line(img, (90,q-5),(110,q-5), color, thickness=1) #add ticks
    cv2.line(img, (90,q+5),(110,q+5), color, thickness=1)
    cv2.line(img, (q+5,q-5),(q-5,q+5), color, thickness=1)
    x=q+50
    cv2.line(img, (100,x),(x,x), color, thickness=1)
    cv2.arrowedLine(img, (50+x//2,x), (60+x//2,x), color, thickness=1, tipLength=1.0) #parallel marker
    pts.extend([(x,x),(100,x)])
for j,lbl in enumerate('ACFDGEB'):
    p=pts[j]
    q=10 if j%2 else -20
    cv2.putText(img,lbl,(p[0]+q,p[1]),font,0.6,color,2)
show_geometry_image(img)
```

::: {#exr-5.7.34}

Below, $\overline{AB}\parallel \overline{EF}\parallel \overline{CD}$. Show that
$$\frac{1}{EF}= \frac{1}{AB}+ \frac{1}{CD}$$
Interestingly, if $AB,CD$ represent the amount of time it takes 1 person and another to do a task individually, then $EF$ is the amount of time it takes them, working together.

:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
img = np.ones((500, 600, 3), dtype=np.uint8) * 255
a=(180,200)
b=(80,400)
c=(530,100)
d=(380,400)
e=get_intersection(a,d,b,c)
f=get_intersection(b,d,e,(e[0]+50,e[1]-100))
draw_path(img,b,c,d,a,b,d)
cv2.line(img,e,f, color, thickness=2)
for j,lbl in enumerate('ABCDEF'):
    p=globals()[lbl.lower()]
    q=20 if j%2 else -15
    cv2.putText(img,lbl,(p[0],p[1]+q),font,0.6,color,2)
for p in [b,d,f]: #parallel markers
    cv2.arrowedLine(img,(p[0]+25,p[1]-50),(p[0]+30,p[1]-60),color,thickness=1,tipLength=1)
show_geometry_image(img)
```
